cards.front: force arrow
cards.back: An arrow that shows a force. Its length shows the size and its direction shows the way the force pushes or pulls.
cards.say: force arrow. An arrow that shows a force. Its length shows the size and its direction shows the way the force pushes or pulls.

cards.front: balanced forces
cards.back: Forces that are equal in size and opposite in direction. Together they have no effect on movement.
cards.say: balanced forces. Forces that are equal in size and opposite in direction. Together they have no effect on movement.

cards.front: unbalanced forces
cards.back: Forces that are not equal. They change how an object moves.
cards.say: unbalanced forces. Forces that are not equal. They change how an object moves.

cards.front: resultant force
cards.back: The single force that has the same effect as all the forces on an object together.
cards.say: resultant force. The single force that has the same effect as all the forces on an object together.

cards.front: What happens to an object at rest when the forces on it are balanced?
cards.back: It stays still.
cards.say: What happens to an object at rest when the forces on it are balanced? It stays still.

cards.front: What happens to a moving object when forces are balanced?
cards.back: It keeps moving at the same speed in a straight line.
cards.say: What happens to a moving object when forces are balanced? It keeps moving at the same speed in a straight line.

cards.front: What can unbalanced forces do to a moving object?
cards.back: Make it speed up, slow down or change direction.
cards.say: What can unbalanced forces do to a moving object? Make it speed up, slow down or change direction.

cards.front: Ten newtons push right and ten newtons push left. What is the resultant force?
cards.back: Zero. The forces are balanced.
cards.say: Ten newtons push right and ten newtons push left. What is the resultant force? Zero. The forces are balanced.

cards.front: Fifteen newtons push right and five newtons push left. What is the resultant force?
cards.back: Ten newtons to the right. Subtract the smaller from the larger.
cards.say: Fifteen newtons push right and five newtons push left. What is the resultant force? Ten newtons to the right. Subtract the smaller from the larger.

cards.front: Twenty newtons pull up and twenty newtons pull down. What happens?
cards.back: The forces are balanced, so the object does not move.
cards.say: Twenty newtons pull up and twenty newtons pull down. What happens? The forces are balanced, so the object does not move.

cards.front: Which direction does a resultant force make an object accelerate?
cards.back: In the direction of the larger force.
cards.say: Which direction does a resultant force make an object accelerate? In the direction of the larger force.

cards.front: weight
cards.back: The pull of gravity on an object. It acts downwards.
cards.say: weight. The pull of gravity on an object. It acts downwards.

cards.front: upthrust
cards.back: The upward push of water on an object in it.
cards.say: upthrust. The upward push of water on an object in it.

cards.front: Why does a boat float?
cards.back: Its weight is balanced by the upthrust of the water.
cards.say: Why does a boat float? Its weight is balanced by the upthrust of the water.

cards.front: Why does a stone sink?
cards.back: Its weight is bigger than the upthrust, so the forces are unbalanced and the stone goes down.
cards.say: Why does a stone sink? Its weight is bigger than the upthrust, so the forces are unbalanced and the stone goes down.

cards.front: thrust
cards.back: A force that pushes a vehicle forward, such as from an engine.
cards.say: thrust. A force that pushes a vehicle forward, such as from an engine.

cards.front: drag
cards.back: A force from air or water that acts against a moving object. It is also called resistance.
cards.say: drag. A force from air or water that acts against a moving object. It is also called resistance.

cards.front: A car travels at a steady speed. What is true about thrust and drag?
cards.back: They are balanced: they are equal in size and opposite in direction.
cards.say: A car travels at a steady speed. What is true about thrust and drag? They are balanced: they are equal in size and opposite in direction.

cards.front: A car speeds up. What is true about thrust and drag?
cards.back: Thrust is bigger than drag.
cards.say: A car speeds up. What is true about thrust and drag? Thrust is bigger than drag.

cards.front: Why does a falling skydiver stop speeding up?
cards.back: Air resistance grows with speed until it equals the weight. The forces are then balanced and the speed stays steady.
cards.say: Why does a falling skydiver stop speeding up? Air resistance grows with speed until it equals the weight. The forces are then balanced and the speed stays steady.

cards.front: In a tug of war, one team pulls with 800 newtons and the other with 700 newtons. What happens?
cards.back: The first team wins, because the resultant force is 100 newtons in their direction.
cards.say: In a tug of war, one team pulls with 800 newtons and the other with 700 newtons. What happens? The first team wins, because the resultant force is 100 newtons in their direction.

cards.front: contact force
cards.back: A force that acts only when objects touch, such as friction or a push.
cards.say: contact force. A force that acts only when objects touch, such as friction or a push.

cards.front: non-contact force
cards.back: A force that acts without touching, such as gravity or magnetism.
cards.say: non-contact force. A force that acts without touching, such as gravity or magnetism.

cards.front: What does it mean if a force arrow is twice as long as another?
cards.back: The force is twice as big.
cards.say: What does it mean if a force arrow is twice as long as another? The force is twice as big.
